taskDescription: Click every word that names a defining property of the genetic code.
textField: The genetic code is *degenerate* because most amino acids have more than one codon. It is *unambiguous* because each codon specifies only one amino acid. The code is nearly *universal* across all species with few mitochondrial exceptions. Because codons are read without gaps or overlaps, the code is said to be *commaless*, and adding or deleting a single base causes a *frameshift* that alters every downstream codon.

overallFeedback.feedback: Degeneracy (multiple codons per amino acid), unambiguity (one amino acid per codon), universality (the same code in nearly all organisms), commaless reading (no gaps between codons) and frameshift sensitivity (one insertion or deletion disrupts all downstream reading) are the five key properties that explain both the robustness and the vulnerability of translation.
